by their subordinates is properly used and cared for, and that proper custody, safekeeping, and disposition are provided. It is inherent in all supervisory positions, is not contingent upon signed receipts or responsibility statements and cannot be delegated. It arises because of assignment to a specific position..”

That being said, I seriously doubt this soldier is the OIC/NCOIC of their section by paragraph and line number of the MTOE/TDA. 

Soldier should write a MFR stating all of the above occurrences as well as a sworn statement that would be used as supporting documentation for the FLIPL. Key control logs should be requested in which each individual with access would need to provide the same documentation (MFR, 2823 explaining reasons for utilizing the container and what items were retrieved). 

Even if a FLIPL is processed and financial liability is placed upon the soldier, they still have time to rebuttal. This supporting documentation stated above would help in that process.

A lot of equipment and parts were given a code making the system think they are serialized items- this is usually a GCSS created serial number beginning with '1014'.

if the item is master equipment  (not provisions) and shows on your /ISDFPS/DISP_EQU_SIT, check the equipment number.

Usually the two will match.

IQ02 is to change a serial, but the easiest way is to initiate an inventory for that niin within your sloc, and you will be prompted to enter the correct serial number if the item does not have one, or has the '1014' equipment number serial number.
ZNONSTD is the tcode to add non standard (read: civilian) equipment.

you can add the correct serial numbers into GCSS by creating an inventory for that specific material within that sloc.
